p.PACKAGE-INSTALLS-THE-PERIODIC-HEALTH-AUD: A vibevm `flow` package that installs the **periodic health audit** into a project: a recurring, judgment-heavy sweep over everything the per-commit gate is structurally blind to — uncovered code, out-of-gate trees, drift, and slow debt — recorded as an append-only trend in `AUDIT.md`.

p.THE-GATE-AND-THE-AUDIT-ANSWER-DIFFERENT-: Where the gate answers *"did this commit regress covered code?"*, the audit answers *"what is wrong, rotting, or drifting that no commit will ever flag?"*.

p.THE-GATE-IS-THE-FLOOR-THE-AUDIT-IS-WHAT-: The gate is the floor; the audit is what the gate cannot see.

p.A-MILESTONE-IS-NEVER-DECLARED-DONE-ON-AN: A milestone is never declared done on an un-audited base.

p.package-contents-lead: This package ships three flow documents, a skill, and a boot snippet:

item.CONTENT-THE-PROTOCOL: `spec/flows/health-audit/HEALTH-AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md` — what the audit is and is not, the four blind spots, `AUDIT.md` as the durable home, dispositions and carry-forward, the living-checklist law, the "why not" section, and a re-derive prompt.

item.CONTENT-THE-AUDIT-CHECKLIST: `spec/flows/health-audit/audit-checklist.md` — the categories walked each run (A test integrity, B rot outside the gate, C drift, D debt), every sub-item with what to look for, a mechanical aid, and what "bad" looks like.

item.CONTENT-RUNNING-AN-AUDIT: `spec/flows/health-audit/running-an-audit.md` — the seven-step run, the `AUDIT.md` section format, and a worked example on an invented generic project.

item.CONTENT-THE-SKILL: `spec/skills/health-audit/SKILL.md` — the `health-audit` skill: an agent walks the checklist and drafts the `AUDIT.md` section for approval.

item.CONTENT-THE-BOOT-SNIPPET: `spec/boot/42-flow-health-audit.md` — boot snippet loaded at session start: the one-line law, the cadence, and the never-do list.

p.UNINSTALL-REMOVES-EVERY-FILE-THE-PACKAGE: Uninstalling removes every file the package wrote, including the boot snippet.

p.AUDIT-MD-IS-PROJECT-STATE-NOT-PACKAGE-ST: `AUDIT.md` is **project state** — the package never creates, deletes, or overwrites it as part of install or uninstall.

item.COMPOSES-CAMPAIGN-PLANS: `flow:campaign-plans` — a P1 finding too large to fix in-run is *filed*, and often becomes the seed of the next campaign's mandate: the audit inventories, the campaign drains.

item.COMPOSES-WAL: `flow:wal` — the audit *reconciles* the WAL/checkpoint's known-issues list against its findings, but the findings do **not** live there. The checkpoint is volatile; `AUDIT.md` is the durable, append-only home.

item.COMPOSES-DECISION-RECORDS: `flow:decision-records` — an `accepted` disposition is a decision record: it carries a why and a revisit trigger, not just a shrug.

item.COMPOSES-ATTRIBUTION-POLICY: `flow:git-attribution-policy` — its periodic-audit line item is exactly one row on this checklist: grep the attribution pattern set over surfaces added since the last audit.

p.practice-crystallized-in-the-origin-proj: The practice crystallized in the origin project's periodic-health-audit law, written after a milestone shipped green — every commit passing, hundreds of tests passing — while the initializer scaffolded broken projects and a test asserted the broken output as correct.

p.NO-AMOUNT-OF-GATE-CATCHES-A-TEST-THAT-GU: No amount of gate catches a test that guards a bug; only a periodic judgment sweep does.

p.collections-spirit-is-the-redbook: The collection's spirit is the book *AI-native development*, which ships in Russian inside `flow:redbook` at `spec/book/ru/`: the gate proves the machine did not regress; the audit is where human and agent judgment reads what the machine cannot.
